Atomically Rotate the Master Encryption Key of a PII Vault

Source: R/pii.R
pii_vault_rotate_key.Rd

Authenticates and decrypts an existing airgapllm_vault_v2 (or legacy v1) vault file using old_key, updates the vault key fingerprint under new_key, and atomically re-encrypts the vault at rest using fresh RFC 5869 HKDF-SHA256 subkeys, a brand-new 128-bit random salt, a fresh 128-bit random IV, AAD-bound HMAC-SHA256 authentication, and owner-only (0600) file permissions. All existing token-to-value mappings are preserved so previously pseudonymized outputs remain re-identifiable with new_key.

Usage

pii_vault_rotate_key(path, old_key, new_key, out_path = path, backup = FALSE)

Arguments

path

Character scalar path to the existing encrypted vault file.

old_key

Current secret key used to authenticate and decrypt path.

new_key

New secret key (e.g., from pii_vault_key()) used to re-encrypt the vault. Must differ from old_key.

out_path

Destination file path for the rotated vault. Defaults to path (in-place atomic replacement via temporary file + rename).

backup

Logical scalar; if TRUE and out_path == path, preserves a 0600 backup copy at paste0(path, ".bak") prior to replacement. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A list with path, vault_id, old_key_fingerprint, new_key_fingerprint, n_tokens, and rotated_at.

Examples

k1 <- pii_vault_key()
k2 <- pii_vault_key()
vf <- tempfile(fileext = ".vault.json")
pse <- pii_pseudonymize("Patient Jane Doe (jane@example.org)", key = k1, vault_path = vf)
rot <- pii_vault_rotate_key(vf, old_key = k1, new_key = k2)
rot$new_key_fingerprint
#> [1] "fd52d0a2d4ab8b8a"
pii_reidentify(pse$text, vault = vf, key = k2)
#> [1] "Patient Jane Doe (jane@example.org)"
unlink(vf)
